paper.title_en: Universal Scaling Function for Giant-Graviton Operator Product Expansion Coefficients
paper.abstract_en: We consider the large-spin limit <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>∞</mi></mrow></math> of the operator product expansion (OPE) coefficient for two maximal giant gravitons and a spinning operator with finite twist in planar <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> super-Yang-Mills theory. Up to an overall normalization factor, this OPE coefficient exhibits a power-law scaling of the form <math display="inline"><msup><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></math>. We provide strong evidence that the exponent <math display="inline"><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> is free from finite-size corrections. Consequently, the all-loop asymptotic expression for the OPE coefficient can be used to determine <math display="inline"><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> exactly. We compute a conjectural expression for the scaling function <math display="inline"><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> for arbitrary values of the ’t Hooft coupling <math display="inline"><mi>g</mi></math>. At weak coupling, our result agrees perfectly with the available field-theoretic results up to three-loop order. At strong coupling, we present the first three orders as concrete predictions. We further provide the finite-coupling result and show that it interpolates smoothly between the weak- and strong-coupling regimes.
